summary: Visual verification accepted non-semantic fallback content, and renderer publication and URL handling were not strict enough.
Evaluation and SkillOpt isolation admitted identity or content aliases and did not bind every input strongly enough.
Review and packaging receipts had overly broad exclusions, mutable-worktree and publication-race exposure, and incomplete exact-schema boundaries.
Scheduler reviews were not causally bound to source observation events, timestamp ordering was ambiguous, and ordinary engineering requests could be misrouted.
Aggregate phase labels could promote mixed evidence, and reviewer task identities were described too strongly as authorship proof.
remediation: Implemented in the candidate worktree; none of these fixes count as accepted until new exact-payload code, frozen-spec, and three-panel architecture-council reviews pass with no unresolved actionables.
claim_boundary: This record preserves the failed first review. It is not a passing review receipt and cannot satisfy AC-24.
